acceptance_test_matrix: Tumbling event-time windows assign records to fixed intervals and emit exactly once when watermark passes window end.
Sliding event-time windows assign records to all overlapping windows and close each eligible window deterministically on watermark advancement.
Processing-time windows use trigger semantics and do not require watermark movement to close.
Watermark-only advancement closes eligible event-time windows without requiring a later data record.
Late arrivals are dropped when configured to drop and admitted only until the allowed-lateness bound when configured to allow lateness.
Per-partition state isolation is asserted so identical keys in different partitions do not share windows or aggregate state.
Invalid or stale timestamps and invariant-failure paths do not corrupt open or already emitted window state.
Failure or partial acceptance paths reject a bad late or invalid event while continuing to accept later valid events and close future windows.
Zero-allocation hot-path intent is covered by implementation review and available allocation-sensitive QA gates.
Benchmark surface includes WindowedAggregateNode and jmhSmokeCheck is green.
Configured QA gates qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh pass.
assumptions: Existing runtime-core watermark APIs are the integration point for event-time advancement and watermark-only closure.
Processing-time windows use the existing runtime clock or timer abstraction rather than direct wall-clock reads in core node logic.
Window state belongs to each graph partition and must never be shared or merged across partitions.
Session windows and custom user-defined windows are out of scope for R-001.
Benchmark smoke coverage can be added under the existing benchmarks surface and verified through jmhSmokeCheck.

critic.rationale: The plan satisfies the blocking lifecycle, QA sequencing, review, verification, and human-gated merge requirements. The main weaknesses are advisory: non-terminal slices are not explicitly routed to a historian/final handoff, and the roadmap scope names session windows while the plan narrows them out of scope without explicitly recording that as a dependency/scope decision beyond assumptions and forbidden alternatives.

acceptance_tests: Tumbling event-time windows aggregate records into exact fixed intervals and emit exactly once when the watermark passes the window end.
Sliding event-time windows assign each record to all expected overlapping windows and close each eligible window independently and deterministically on watermark advancement.
Processing-time windows close through runtime clock or timer trigger semantics without relying on event-time watermark movement.
Watermark-only advancement closes eligible windows even when no later data record arrives.
Late arrivals are dropped after close when policy is drop and are admitted only until the configured allow-lateness horizon when policy allows lateness.
Per-partition isolation is verified by identical keys and timestamps on separate partitions with no cross-partition aggregation leakage.
Invalid or stale timestamps and invariant-failure paths do not corrupt open or already emitted window state.
Rejected late or invalid events do not prevent later valid events from being accepted and future windows from closing correctly.
jmhSmokeCheck includes a WindowedAggregateNode benchmark surface and passes.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: WindowedAggregateNode must execute only inside the owning GraphPartitionRunner partition thread. Window state is scoped to one partition, never shared globally, and close decisions must be deterministic for a fixed input order, partition id, clock mode, and watermark sequence.
forbidden_alternatives: Do not implement session windows.
Do not implement custom user-defined windows.
Do not add cross-partition window merging or a global shared window map.
Do not close event-time windows only during data-record ingestion while ignoring watermark-only advancement.
Do not allocate boxed keys or per-event temporary collections on the aggregation hot path.
Do not introduce durable snapshot, CRC, journal, or recovery machinery for this non-durability feature.
Do not change QA smoke scripts to skip failing coverage instead of implementing the feature.
hard_constraints: Support tumbling and sliding windows only.
Support event-time and processing-time timestamp selection.
Watermark advancement must close eligible event-time windows without requiring arrival of a later data record.
Late-arrival policy must distinguish drop from allow-lateness behavior and enforce the configured lateness horizon.
Aggregation state must use Agrona-style zero-allocation collections on the hot path.
Window state must be per-partition and never cross-partition.
